sections.title: The Completion of the Tabernacle
observations: Exodus 40 marks the culmination of the instructions given to Moses regarding the construction of the Tabernacle, the dwelling place of God among His people. The meticulous details provided in previous chapters are now brought to fruition, emphasizing the importance of obedience to God's commands.

The setting up of the Tabernacle signifies God's desire to dwell among His people, illustrating the theme of God's presence throughout the book of Exodus. This act of completion is not merely a physical construction but a spiritual milestone for Israel.

sections.title: The Anointing of the Tabernacle and Its Furnishings
observations: Moses is commanded to anoint the Tabernacle and all its furnishings, which signifies their consecration for holy use. This act of anointing is crucial as it sets apart these items for God's service, highlighting the sacredness of worship and the need for purity in approaching God.
The anointing also foreshadows the coming of Christ, who is the ultimate anointed one, fulfilling the role of priest and king.

sections.title: The Glory of the Lord Fills the Tabernacle
observations: The climax of this chapter is the descent of God's glory, represented by the cloud, filling the Tabernacle. This event signifies God's approval of the Tabernacle and His presence among His people. It serves as a powerful reminder of God's holiness and the seriousness of His dwelling among sinful humanity.
The cloud also serves as a guide for the Israelites, illustrating how God leads His people and the importance of following His direction.

importantVerses.commentary: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. This verse highlights the divine presence and approval of God, marking the significance of the Tabernacle as a place of worship and communion with God.

questions: What does the construction and anointing of the Tabernacle teach us about the nature of worship?
How does the presence of God's glory in the Tabernacle relate to our understanding of God's presence in our lives today?
In what ways does the Tabernacle foreshadow the coming of Christ and the establishment of the new covenant?
